changes.text: On Windows, new installations default to HarkenStudioHub directly under Program Files, and the main application and setup use the HarkenStudioHub name. Existing installation locations and older Studio launchers remain supported.
Windows desktop shortcuts and taskbar icons now display the H logo with crisp images for different icon sizes.
Project association prompts in Engine Integrations now refer only to Unity projects.
Hub uses the gradient Harken Studio logo and matching H window and tray icons, and consistently displays Harken Studio Hub in menus, notifications, dialogs, and installer details.
Hub displays the Harken Studio logo above a separate Hub label, updates its window title and repository link, and removes the previous application icon.
Project format incompatibility messages show the selected Studio version and the project and Studio Schema versions from the compatibility check.
Hub and Studio updates preserve each other's progress when running together, and outdated operations cannot overwrite newer update state.
Manual and background Studio downloads can run together. Packages remain protected from competing downloads and cache cleanup until installation handoff finishes.
Updates and local build checks recover from temporary file locks on Windows without reporting unsaved state as complete.
Studio installation, repair, and removal recover when Windows briefly locks the installation index.
Reopening a project in a compatible Studio version activates its existing window, and Hub recognizes a successful handoff.
Choose SDKs bundled with installed Studio versions directly from the SDK source dropdown. Click anywhere in the field to open the list, or browse for another folder.

SDK checks show version changes and file counts grouped by addition, update, removal, and preservation. Preserved files are collapsed, and a separate check log highlights failures, warnings, and recommended actions.
New Studio installations use shorter folder names without lengthy build identifiers. Different builds of the same version can still be installed side by side.
Windows now displays the application name without an additional description.
Engine Integrations uses system file and folder pickers, restoring address-bar path navigation on Windows.
Hub and Studio updates now use the new GitHub repository, with COS downloads retained as a fallback.
SDK integration retries temporary file locks on Windows instead of failing immediately.
Unreal SDK installation now rejects incomplete native headers before changing the game project.
